target_customer: HR leaders and employers paying per employee for perks, rewards and recognition software
problem: Companies of any size wanted big-company style employee perks and recognition without building their own program. AnyPerk started as a discount marketplace and grew into rewards and recognition.
business_model: B2B SaaS per employee per month
product_category: Employee rewards, recognition and perks platform

founders.name: Taro Fukuyama
previous_startups: Mieple, dating site idea the founders first applied to YC with (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Sunny Tsang
previous_startups: Mieple, dating site idea the founders first applied to YC with (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Role listed on the YC page as founder and chief designer. Education and prior employers not found.

competitors.name: BetterWorks (early perks concept)
competitors.what: Similar employee perks concept; a TechCrunch piece noted it had raised $10.5M and shut down in May 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: A perks and deals portal was mostly web CRUD plus vendor negotiation; the hard part was business development with merchants, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Discount catalogs were copyable, and a 2016 Business Insider piece noted rivals offered similar perks. Later recognition workflows added some switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Reward Gateway, an established employee engagement vendor, acquired Fond in 2023 after about a decade of independent operation.

market_need_then: In 2012 the product began as web service discounts for startups, copying the perks YC gives its own companies; the CEO later said the main competitor was HR departments building internal programs.

branding.name_origin: AnyPerk named after the perks it delivers. Fond (2017) was chosen to signal affection, joy and affinity employers cultivate in employees, picked by the senior team with a naming consultant from 140 trademark-cleared names.
branding.domain_note: fond.co used after the 2017 rename; it now redirects to rewardgateway.com.

rebrands.why: Company said the old name no longer fit a mission and product line broader than perks

brand_strength.rationale: Rename sources are company statements and a naming consultant's write-up; no sources show consumer awareness or community around the brand.

pivots.to: discounts on web services for startups (AnyPerk)
pivots.why: Founders went through six pivots in the first month of YC, per a Priceonomics-style profile

pivots.to: employee perks sold per employee to companies
pivots.why: Larger and recurring market; reported pricing about five dollars per employee per month

outcome_analysis: AnyPerk pivoted from a startup discount list to an employee perks subscription, raised an $8.5M Series A in 2015 and a $11.5M Series A-1 in 2016, renamed to Fond in 2017 as it moved into rewards and recognition, and was acquired by Reward Gateway in early 2023. Sources do not state a price, so the exit quality is unknown.
notes: fond.co fetch returned a 301 redirect to rewardgateway.com (site is the acquirer's now). Acquisition date: YC news item and one profile say 2023-02-28, PrivSource lists 2023-03-01. Seed amount from a Vator headline of $3M; a PYMNTS headline mentions $4.5M, possibly cumulative, unverified. Total raised varies by aggregator (12.9M to 24.5M), unverified. Series A-1 stage labelled series_a because the company calls it Series A-1.
